caption:
foundit's appraisal survey puts it plainly: 52% of India's professionals are already job-hunting, and 96% say they're open to switching.

That is not a competence problem. Most of those people are good at the work. They lost the room in a twenty-minute review conversation — hedging the ask, under-claiming the year, letting a manager's pause fill with their own apology.

October to December is positioning season. Half-yearly reviews land now. The January-April appraisal round is decided by the impression you set in the next ten weeks, not by the slide deck you build in March.

Three things to fix before then. Bearing: sit like the work is already yours. Tone: drop the upward lilt at the end of a sentence, it turns a statement into a request. Silence: after you state your number, stop talking. The next person to speak concedes.

Command is a practice. Rehearse it before the meeting, not during it.

topic.title: Appraisal churn: 52% job-hunting, 96% open to switching
topic.angle: This is the statistical portrait of being passed over — half the market is leaving because of a review conversation lost to hedging and under-claiming, not to lack of competence.
topic.why_now: October–December is when Indian firms run half-yearly reviews and people start positioning for the January–April appraisal round, making this a preparation-season play rather than breaking news (the foundit report dates to late July 2026).

rationale: A stark, text-only stat card matches the no-nonsense tone and lets the two numbers carry the argument without visual decoration.
